feed.title: NPR Programs: All Things Considered
feed.subtitle: All Things Considered hosts Ailsa Chang, Mary Louise Kelly, Juana Summers and Scott Detrow present the program's trademark mix of news, interviews, commentaries, reviews, and offbeat features 7 days a week.

entry.title: Israeli president invites Netanyahu's opposition leader to broker new government
entry.summary: Israel's political landscape shifts as President Herzog hands opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot the mandate to form a government, dealing a blow to Benjamin Netanyahu's grip on power.

entry.title: Texas's 'Blue Tsunami' has former Texas congressman Beto O'Rourke 'over the moon'
entry.summary: NPR's Rob Schmitz speaks with former Texas congressman Beto O'Rourke about how past efforts by him and other Democrats helped the party win big in Texas in the midterms.

entry.title: The surprising and often forgotten history of economic populism in Texas
entry.summary: NPR's Rob Schmitz speaks with Austin-based political commentator David Griscom. He authored a book titled The Myth of Red Texas which tells the story of economic populism in Texas.

entry.title: A correspondent finds Cuba's people struggling
entry.summary: Reporting from Cuba comes with distinct challenges especially amid widespread power outages and fuel shortages.

entry.title: How painter Maira Kalman finds 'Joy' in darkness
entry.summary: Author and painter Maira Kalman is out with a new book called Joy, exploring all the things that bring her fleeting happiness and why sorrow is a necessary counterpart to joy.

entry.title: President of The Heritage Foundation looks ahead to the future of the GOP
entry.summary: Kevin Roberts, the president of the conservative think tank The Heritage Foundation, talks about the organization's priorities and hopes for the future of the Republican Party and its policies.

entry.title: Oklahoma tribes says proposed legal changes puts ancestral lands in Ohio at risk
entry.summary: The Trump administration has proposed changes to the National Historic Preservation Act that could endanger historic sites that are significant to tribal nations across the country. Oklahoma tribes say that puts ancestral lands in Ohio at risk.

entry.title: How a musician turned singing sands into an instrument
entry.summary: A North Carolina musician was fascinating by the sound of singing sand dunes. He asked researchers from all over the world for help turning them into an instrument.

entry.title: Housing affordability after the midterm elections
entry.summary: Housing affordability was a big issue for voters who helped sweep Democrats into power this week. Tackling it will take time.

entry.title: American democracy was a big winner in the midterms
entry.summary: Results are still outstanding House and Senate races but political scientists say one of the big winners in the mid-terms is American democracy itself.
